text:
Priya N.: Hi team — baby arrived early! :baby: I need to add the newborn to medical and dependent FSA but the hospital says the official birth certificate will take 6-8 weeks. What can I upload now to get coverage started?
Lina (People Ops): Congrats, Priya!! :tada: You qualify for a QLE. Carriers accept provisional docs while you wait for the birth certificate.
Priya N.: What counts as provisional? Hospital discharge papers?
Benefits Admin: For newborns we accept hospital birth record / discharge summary + infant temporary SSN application receipt OR a signed physician statement. Ideally two items: one primary (hospital record) + one secondary (SSN app or pediatrician note).
Priya N.: I only have the hospital discharge and the baby’s temporary SSN application receipt (hospital filed it). Is that enough?
Lina (People Ops): Yes that's sufficient to provisionally enroll. Upload both and select "New dependent - birth". You'll need to send the final birth certificate within 60 days to finalize. If final docs aren’t received carriers can retroactively deny coverage.
Priya N.: Secure place to upload? Don't want to email PHI.
people-ops-bot: Secure upload link: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload/PN-1876503210 (expires in 14 days).
Priya N.: Uploading now. Do I need to do anything in the benefits portal?
Lina (People Ops): Yes after upload go to Benefits > Manage Dependents and start "Add dependent due to QLE" flow. Choose plans (medical + FSA) and indicate effective date = date of birth.
Ken L.: Payroll note: if you enroll mid-cycle we’ll prorate premiums and adjust paycheck. For FSA, election changes are allowed for a QLE; we'll update deductions starting next payroll after benefits confirms enrollment.
Priya N.: For FSA, can I elect the full year amount now or pro-rate?
Benefits Admin: You can elect the annual amount and payroll will prorate the per-paycheck deduction based on when the change takes effect. If you want a custom prorate, put that request in the notes and we'll check with payroll.
Priya N.: Is a scanned photo of the hospital record ok? It has the hospital letterhead and signature.
Lina (People Ops): Scanned photo is fine as long as it's legible and includes the newborn's name, DOB, and hospital info. Avoid phone glare on the signature area if possible.
Priya N.: If I can't get the birth certificate within 60 days because of county backlog, what happens?
Benefits Admin: If there's a known delay, upload county receipt or correspondence showing processing delays and we'll request an extension with the carrier. Keep us updated; we handle most extensions case-by-case.
Priya N.: Thanks. Should I include baby's name as "Infant" on uploads until certificate is official?
Lina (People Ops): Use the legal name you're using on hospital paperwork. If name changes later, we can update after final docs. Using "Infant" can complicate carrier verification.
Priya N.: Uploaded both docs and started portal flow. Tag me when confirmed?
people-ops-bot: Case created: PO-7383 - Newborn provisional enrollment.
Ken L.: I'll monitor payroll once benefits confirms. Expect confirmation email within 2 business days.
Priya N.: Appreciate it all :heart:
